extracted.intended_audience: open governance practitioners, policymakers, civil-society organisations, and partners interested in adaptive learning
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and evaluating an organisational 'learning plan' that uses adaptive learning (theory-informed, data-driven, reflective practice) to improve impact on open governance and related reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive learning (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptive learning is a structured process of learning by doing: a continuous process of theoretically-informed, data-driven, reflection and adaptation, aimed at improving impact and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasises the full cycle — theory-informed design, collection/analysis of data, structured reflection, and adaptation of practice — as the core component of the approach. Reference to a 'Figure. The cycle of adaptive learning' indicates an iterative loop; use all elements together rather than isolated monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the theory of change explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit the theory of change at the heart of the learning plan so that learning and adaptation are guided by a clear causal logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The learning plan 'sets out how we are implementing and exploring this theory of change'; the guidance is to articulate assumptions and pathways so reflection can test and refine them, and to use that explicit theory to sharpen impact and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally-led, best-fit approaches (avoid one-size-fits-all)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainable change comes through locally-led efforts to craft and implement best-fit approaches, rather than through implementation of best-practice blueprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise locally appropriate experimentation and tailoring over importing fixed 'best practice' models. The plan should support local actors to design and test context-specific solutions and adjust based on learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage political dynamics and strengthen reform coalitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptive learning should engage the political dynamics of development, strengthen reform coalitions, and inform political action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning activities to surface and respond to political constraints/opportunities; measure and support coalition-building and political effects, not only technical outputs. Treat political engagement as central to adaptation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use learning to bridge commitments and implementation (focus on results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptive learning provides a means of navigating complexity, closing the gap between policy commitments and implementation, addressing delivery challenges and delivering results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame learning activities around improving implementation and outcomes. Track whether adaptations are narrowing the implementation gap and producing demonstrable delivery improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalise learning at organisational and individual levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice adaptive learning not only through programmes and projects but also at the organisational and individual levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed routines, incentives and capacities for learning inside the organisation (e.g., staff practice, management processes) as well as within external projects, so learning is sustained and scaled across the organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative revision and continuous refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the learning plan and refine activities in light of structured reflection and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the plan itself as provisional: regularly review findings, incorporate feedback, and update strategies. The page states 'We will revise it and refine what we do in the light of that reflection.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a framework for reflection and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The learning plan should provide a clear framework to structure reflection and learning processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the plan to guide when and how teams reflect, what questions to ask, what evidence to collect, and how to decide on adaptations. The framework should make reflection systematic rather than ad hoc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate data and citizen engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Support adaptive learning through activities on data and citizen engagement (collecting and using data, and engaging citizens in governance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalise data collection/use and citizen participation as key inputs into reflection and adaptation. Examples cited include work on integrity in different countries and projects focused on data-driven citizen engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work through multi-stakeholder governance initiatives and thematic programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Support adaptive learning through multi-stakeholder governance initiatives (including the Open Government Partnership) and thematic programmes such as open fiscal governance and money in politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage partnerships and multi-stakeholder fora to design, test and scale adaptations. The page lists program areas (multi-stakeholder initiatives, fiscal governance, campaign finance, etc.) as channels for practicing adaptive learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit and share feedback with communities of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively seek feedback and engage with wider communities of practice to learn from peers and share lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors invite feedback and participation (e.g., Adaptive Development Google Group, communities like Doing Development Differently). Use peer feedback and cross-organisational exchange to surface challenges, successes, and transferable learning.
